frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Being in — or being brought into — a SOUND, FIT, UN-SPOILED right-working condition: intactness / fitness-for-purpose / rightly-ordered wholeness, defined as the positive opposite of fasad (spoilage/corruption). The root itself supplies only this notion of "sound/right condition"; whether it appears as a state (be sound), a quality (that which is sound/fit), or a causation (make sound / set right) is contributed by form, not by the root.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Being in — or being brought into — a SOUND, FIT, UN-SPOILED right-working condition: intactness / fitness-for-purpose / rightly-ordered wholeness, defined as the positive opposite of fasad (spoilage/corruption). internal_discovery.plain_explanation:
Every form-family recovers the same core "soundness / right-fit condition," differing only by the morphology layered on top.

FORM I (stative) — 13:23 and 40:8 "wa-man salaha min aabaaihim" ("whoever WAS sound/in-right-condition among their forefathers"): the bare verb is the intransitive state of being sound/fit, here fit to enter the Gardens. This is the clearest window on the root: to be in sound order.

PARTICIPLE saalih / saalihaat / saalihuun (the bulk, N/ADJ) — the one/thing IN that sound condition. Applied to deeds: "a deed that is sound/proper/fit" ("aamalan saalihan" 18:110; "al-aamal al-saalih" 35:10; "al-saalihaat" throughout with amiluu). Applied to persons: "sound/upright ones" (12:101, 21:75, 4:69). Crucially the same participle is used non-morally: "in aataytanaa saalihan" (7:189-190) = "if You give us a SOUND [well-formed] child"; "kaana abuuhumaa saalihan" (18:82); "takuunuu qawman saalihiin" (12:9) = "you will become a people in good/sound standing" after removing Joseph. These physical/relational uses show the residue is soundness-of-condition, not merely piety.

FORM IV aslaha / islaah / muslih (causative) — "put/bring into sound condition." With a plain object: "yuslih lakum aamaalakum" (33:71, set your deeds right), "aslaha baalahum" (47:2, 47:5, set their state right), "aslahnaa lahu zawjahu" (21:90, made his wife sound/fit to bear), "laa yuslihu aamala l-mufsidiin" (10:81, God will not make sound the corrupters' work), "aslih lii fii dhurriyyatii" (46:15). Absolutely (after repentance): "taabuu wa-aslahuu" (2:160, 3:89, 4:146, 5:39, 24:5, 16:119, 6:48, 6:54, 7:35) = "repented and set [themselves] right." With the construction bayna: "aslaha baynahum" / "aslihuu bayna" (2:182, 2:224, 4:35, 4:128, 49:9, 49:10, 8:1, 4:114) = bring the between-relation into sound order = reconcile. The verbal noun islaah (2:220 orphans, 2:228, 4:35, 7:56/7:85 "after its islaah/setting-in-order") and the agent muslih/muslihuun (2:11, 11:117, 28:19, 7:170, 2:220) name the setting-right and the setter-right.

THE INTERNAL ANCHOR: SlH stands in explicit, repeated opposition to FSD (fasad/mufsiduun). "laa tufsiduu fii l-ardi baada islaahihaa" (7:56, 7:85: do not SPOIL the land after its being SET-RIGHT); "innamaa nahnu muslihuun" answering "laa tufsiduu" (2:11); "yufsiduuna fii l-ardi wa-laa yuslihuun" (26:152, 27:48); "al-mufsida mina l-muslih" (2:220); "amiltum al-saalihaat ... ka-l-mufsidiin" (38:28). This antonym pair fixes the direction: SlH = un-spoiled sound right-order; FSD = spoilage/corruption. Because fasad covers both moral and physical/functional spoiling, salaah correspondingly covers moral righteousness AND physical/relational soundness under one center.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions performed to isolate the residue: (a) FORM — Form I gives the intransitive STATE (be sound); Form IV gives CAUSATION (make sound / set right); the active participle saalih gives the QUALITY-bearer (one who/that which is sound); verbal noun islaah gives the abstract ACT of setting-sound; agent noun muslih the AGENT. Strip all of these and "sound/right condition" remains. (b) CONSTRUCTION — the preposition bayna supplies the relational "between" target, turning "make sound" into "reconcile"; benefactive li- ("aslih lii", "yuslih lakum") supplies the beneficiary; min al-saalihiin supplies partitive membership. None of these belong to the root. (c) PARTICIPANTS — agent may be God (33:71, 21:90, 10:81), prophets (7:142 "wa-aslih"), or ordinary humans (49:9); object may be deeds, a wife, a state (baal), land, offspring, or a social rupture. The residue is invariant across all. (d) CONTEXT — eschatological reward ("aamanuu wa-amiluu l-saalihaat"), family/inheritance law (4:35, 4:128), inter-communal law (49:9), and prophetic narrative are all discourse settings, subtracted. The proper name Salih (PN) freezes the participle saalih ("the sound/righteous one") as a rigid designator: the residue is lexically present in the name but referentially inert (bleached) in context — a naming-layer, not a compositional, presence.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The proper name Salih (Prophet of Thamud): 11:61, 11:62, 11:66, 11:89, 26:142, 27:45, 7:73, 7:75, 7:77 (9 PN occurrences). Here the root makes no compositional contribution to the sentence — the word simply designates a person ("yaa Saalih 'tinaa..." 7:77). This is the hardest case because a rigid designator is semantically bleached: one cannot subtract form/construction/context and be left with an operative "soundness" meaning in the utterance. It RECONCILES rather than contradicts because the name is morphologically identical to the active participle saalih and transparently lexicalizes exactly the root residue ("the sound/upright one"); the soundness sense is thus present at the naming layer and is nowhere negated. It is not placed in inconsistent_refs because the residue is recoverable (indeed etymologically transparent) and never contradicted — only referentially dormant. This is the single point that keeps the disposition from being maximally clean.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative center: "moral righteousness / doing pious good." It fits the dominant collocation "aamanuu wa-amiluu l-saalihaat" and "al-saalihiin" (the righteous) very naturally. Internal evidence arbitrates AGAINST it as the core, because SlH is applied where no moral-piety reading is available: "aslahnaa lahu zawjahu" (21:90, making a barren wife FIT to conceive), "in aataytanaa saalihan" (7:189-190, a SOUND child), "baada islaahihaa" of the LAND (7:56, 7:85), "aslih baynahum" (reconciling a dispute, 2:182), "yuslih lakum aamaalakum" (33:71). "Righteousness" cannot cover a fertile womb, arable land, or a repaired quarrel; "soundness/right-order" covers all of these AND yields "righteousness" as its application to persons/deeds. The FSD antonym (which spans physical spoilage and moral corruption alike) confirms the broader center. So the moral reading is a contextual specialization of the induced residue, not the residue itself.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) FSD (fa-sin-dal, corruption/spoilage) — the direct antonym, co-occurring constantly (2:11, 7:56, 26:152, 2:220, 38:28); SlH is precisely the positive pole FSD negates, so they share an axis but oppose in sign. (2) TQY (taqwa, reverent god-fearing) and BRR (birr, dutiful piety) — overlap with SlH only in the "righteous person" application, but denote devotional reverence/dutifulness, whereas SlH denotes functional soundness/fitness-of-condition that need not be devotional (a sound child, fertile wife, ordered land). (3) HSN (husn/ihsan, goodness-excellence-beauty) — often paired ("wa-amiluu l-saalihaat ... yuhibbu l-muhsiniin" 5:93); HSN marks aesthetic/qualitative excellence, whereas SlH marks intact fitness-for-purpose (a deed that WORKS / is proper, not merely a deed that is fine). Falsifiability condition: the hypothesis would fail if some occurrence applied SlH to a thing that is reverent/devout but not sound-in-condition, or to a thing that is beautiful/excellent yet spoiled or non-functional, with no reading of intact right-order available. No such occurrence exists in the 180.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — "sound / fit / un-spoiled right-working condition" — is surface-recoverable across all 180 occurrences and across every form-family: Form I as the state (salaha, 13:23/40:8), the participle as the sound one/thing (saalih/saalihaat/saalihiin, incl. non-moral 7:189-190, 18:82, 21:90-context, 12:9), Form IV as the causation of that condition (aslaha/islaah, incl. land 7:56, wife 21:90, deeds 33:71, reconciliation 49:9), and the agent muslih. The direction is determinate and independently fixed by the pervasive internal antonymy with FSD (spoilage/corruption), which also explains why the sense spans both moral righteousness and physical/relational soundness without splitting. The competing "moral righteousness" center is decisively too narrow (fails on womb, land, quarrel, deeds-set-right) and is better analyzed as a contextual application of the broader residue. The only inferential step is the bleached proper name Salih (9 PN), which reconciles cleanly because the name is the participle itself and its soundness sense, though referentially dormant, is nowhere contradicted. Because no occurrence resists reconciliation by layer-subtraction, inconsistent_refs is empty; the lone soft spot (name-bleaching) is a naming-layer, not a semantic, exception, so STRONG rather than MODERATE is warranted, distinctiveness against FSD/HSN/TQY being sharp.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation attempt: The candidate ('sound/fit/un-spoiled right-working condition, positive opposite of fasad') survives the productive forms with no homonymy or semantic split. All ~120+ N/ADJ deed uses ('amilu al-salihat', 'amila salihan') read as 'sound/right-working deed' and are explicitly antonym-anchored: 9:102 'amalan salihan wa-akhara sayyi'an' (sound vs spoiled deed), 38:28 al-salihat vs al-mufsidin, 10:81 yuslihu vs al-mufsidin. Non-moral/physical uses that could have broken a purely moral reading instead CONFIRM the candidate: 7:189-190 'salihan' = a well-formed child, 18:82 father 'salihan', 12:9 'qawman salihin' = people in sound standing, 21:90 'aslahna lahu zawjahu' = made his wife fit to bear. Form I stative (13:23, 40:8), Form IV causative 'set right / put into sound order' (33:71, 47:2/47:5 'aslaha balahum'), bayna-reconciliation (2:182, 49:9/49:10, 8:1, 4:35/128) and noun sulh (4:128) all reduce to the same center. Distinctiveness OK: the repeated FSD/sayyi' antonym pairing genuinely discriminates SlH ('un-spoiled fitness-for-purpose') from neighbors Hsn (beauty/good), Tyb (purity/wholesomeness), birr (piety), qwm (uprightness). Falsifiable: clear failure condition (an occurrence unrelated to soundness); the productive forms meet none. HARDEST CASE + why it is a real problem: the 9 proper-name occurrences of the prophet Salih (7:73, 7:75, 7:77, 11:61, 11:62, 11:66, 11:89, 26:142, 27:45). Here the word functions as a rigid designator (vocative 'ya Salih', 'akhahum Salihan'); the 'sound-condition' notion is present only etymologically (the name = 'the upright one') but is semantically inert in the sentence and does no active work. The discovery's universal claim that EVERY form-family recovers the same core as active meaning is therefore false for the PN family, and the frozen candidate's own form-schema (state/quality/causation) does not accommodate lexicalized proper names. This is an over-breadth/coverage gap, not a homonymic split — hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rather than REFUTED. The remaining 171 occurrences hold under one unified center.
